scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8871: host_2_1_1_1 (10.2.1.2) reports it has lost everything
beyond its own gateway: every 10.200.0.x server times out, and it cannot reach
host_1_1_1_1 in the other pod either. It CAN still ping its gateway 10.2.1.1.
Pod 1 is unaffected -- host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm normally. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on router_core_2 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_2 ospfd
Mechanism: router_core_2 is pod 2's only way out: switch_dist_2_1's single
  uplink (172.16.0.8/31, area 1) terminates on router_core_2, which as the
  pod-2 ABR carries 10.2.1.0/24 between area 1 and the area-0 backbone. With
  ospfd killed, zebra flushes router_core_2's OSPF routes immediately, so
  pod-2 traffic arriving at router_core_2 has no route and dies there; the
  other routers then age out router_core_2's LSAs and withdraw 10.2.1.0/24.
  Pod 1 (host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> router_core_3 -> farm)
  never transits router_core_2, so it stays healthy.
Localization: router_core_2
Root cause: ospfd not running on router_core_2
Fix: restart FRR on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on router_core_2" -- that is the same fault observed at the
config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).
Unlike the vtysh-provisioned Kath labs, this topology keeps its OSPF config
in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process, not the file), so a
plain restart reloads the full configuration, OSPF re-converges, and pod 2
regains connectivity.
scoring_axes: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on **router_core_2**: its FRR OSPF configuration exists in `/etc/frr/frr.conf` but was never loaded into the running process, leaving the router with a completely empty FRR running configuration — no `router ospf` block, no network statements, no OSPF adjacencies.

**Mechanism:** `router_core_2` sits between the pod-2 distribution switch (`switch_dist_2_1`, the gateway for `host_2_1_1_1`) and the rest of the backbone (router_core_1, router_core_3). With no OSPF process running, router_core_2 forms no OSPF adjacencies on any of its three interfaces. `switch_dist_2_1` therefore has no OSPF neighbors and its routing table contains only its two directly-connected prefixes (`10.2.1.0/24` and `172.16.0.8/31`). When `host_2_1_1_1` sends traffic destined for the server farm (`10.200.0.x`) or pod 1 (`10.1.1.x`), that traffic reaches `switch_dist_2_1` but is immediately dropped — the gateway has no route to any destination beyond its own segment. Simultaneously, the rest of the OSPF domain never learns `10.2.1.0/24`, so even if packets somehow crossed router_core_2, return traffic would fail.

**Localization:** Solely `router_core_2`; all three interfaces (`eth0`/`eth1`/`eth2`) are configured in frr.conf (area 0 backbone links + area 1 link to pod 2) but none are active in OSPF at runtime. Pod 1 is unaffected because `switch_dist_1_1` uplinks to `router_core_1`, which has a healthy running OSPF process.

**Root cause:** The FRR startup configuration on `router_core_2` was not applied to the running daemon (config was wiped or OSPF was removed post-boot without a reload).

**Fix:** On `router_core_2`, reload the saved config — `vtysh -f /etc/frr/frr.conf` — or restart FRR (`service frr restart`). OSPF adjacencies will form and full reachability for pod 2 will restore within seconds.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies router_core_2 as the affected device.
The report explicitly states no OSPF process is running and the running FRR config lacks a router ospf section (i.e., ospfd/OSPF daemon is down).

per_axis.axis: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2
per_axis.rationale: The report calls out pod 1 as unaffected but does not explicitly state the server farm remains healthy/reachable, so it fails to fully note the limited blast radius to pod 2 and the farm.
Recommends reloading the saved FRR config or restarting the FRR service (vtysh -f /etc/frr/frr.conf or service frr restart), which will load OSPF and restore adjacencies.

The investigation log shows router_core_2's running config lacks any OSPF stanza while /etc/frr/frr.conf contains the OSPF configuration, and switch_dist_2_1 reports no OSPF neighbors — these observations support the agent's conclusion that ospfd/OSPF was not active on router_core_2 and caused pod-2 reachability loss. Minor missing explicit daemon-state or full route-list outputs are not material to the linkage presented.
